library.name: City Central Library
library.description:
This library has been serving the community for over 30 years.
It was founded in 1990 with a collection of 10,000 books.
Today, it houses over 500,000 volumes and offers a wide range of services.
The library is a hub for learning, culture, and community engagement.
It hosts regular events such as book clubs, author readings, and children's programs.
library.history:
The library was originally a small storefront on Elm Street.
In 2005, it moved to its current location after a generous donation.
The building was renovated in 2015 to include modern amenities.
Notable events include the 2010 visit by the President and the 2020 virtual book fair.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.summary:
A story of the mysteriously wealthy Jay Gatsby and his love for the beautiful Daisy Buchanan.
Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, the novel explores themes of decadence, idealism, social upheaval, and excess.
The Great Gatsby is widely considered to be a literary masterpiece and a contender for the title of the Great American Novel.

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.author: Harper Lee
books.summary:
The novel is renowned for its warmth and humor, despite dealing with serious issues of rape and racial inequality.
The story is told by Scout Finch, a young girl growing up in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama.
Her father, Atticus Finch, is a lawyer who defends a black man accused of raping a white woman.

books.author: George Orwell
books.summary:
A dystopian novel set in a totalitarian society ruled by Big Brother.
The protagonist, Winston Smith, struggles to maintain his humanity and sanity in a world where independent thinking is a crime.
The book has become a classic of modern literature and a cautionary tale about the dangers of totalitarianism.
